_meta.role: New College Grad - Embedded Firmware Engineer

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32 bare-metal C, custom PCB design in EAGLE, and hardware interfacing over GPIO, I2C, SPI, and UART. Comfortable debugging software-hardware interactions with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and building physical systems end to end from schematic to firmware. Experienced working in cross-discipline teams spanning electrical, mechanical, and software engineering to bring custom hardware to life.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display, programming peripherals directly at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with no HAL.

Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override; used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination and integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via a TCA9548A I2C mux on a Jetson+Arduino controller.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
